newsitem.title: UK: Ex-UK chancellor Clarke sees stg getting stronger.
newsitem.headline: Ex-UK chancellor Clarke sees stg getting stronger.

text.p: Former Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Tuesday that sterling was likely to rise further as Bank of England Governor Eddie George takes advantage of his new-found freedom to raise interest rates.
Clarke told Channel Four television that his successor, Gordon Brown, would have been better advised "for the time being" to keep control over interest rates.

"Their problem is, they've given Eddie (George) the liberty to keep putting up interest rates as quickly as he wants. He'll make the pound stronger, which is our biggest problem at the moment," Clarke said on the eve of Brown's maiden budget.
Clarke said windfalls from the demutualisation of building societies were troubling an otherwise healthy economic landscape.
"You have strong growth, you have falling unemployment -- you do have to keep that under control," he said.

But Clarke said it was wrong to talk about a crisis fuelled by runaway consumer spending and accused Brown of dreaming up "bogus reasons" for raising taxes now so he could spend more later this parliament in "a cynical attempt to get re-elected".
"They're trying to invent reasons for raising taxation which have nothing to do with the growth of consumer spending," Clarke said.
